topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning outcomes and sets the context for studying cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and Experimental Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the historical discovery of viral and cellular transforming genes alongside the experimental assays used to test cell transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, Tumor Suppressors, and Cell Cycle Regulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the classifications, genetic mechanisms, and cell cycle targets of oncogenic and tumor-suppressive mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Types of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the underlying DNA repair failures, replication errors, and mitotic defects that drive sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multistep Genetic Progression in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic illustrates the stepwise accumulation of driver mutations during colorectal tumorigenesis using the Vogelstein model.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predisposition and Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore inherited cancer predisposition syndromes and their role in accelerating tumor evolution.

topics.label: Conclusion and Further Reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks, student question session, and reading recommendations for the lecture.
